rule: GOAL: Arrange four colored pieces in the middle row to match the top reference pattern. CONTROLS: Click a piece in the bottom tray to select it. Click a middle slot to swap the selected piece into that position. Space was unused. RULE: The top row defines the required color order; matching it clears the level. TRAP: Assuming clicking empty slots or Space performs useful actions wastes moves; only selection and placement matter.

GOAL: Move the red dot to the crosshair by clicking right. CONTROLS: Clicking right moves the dot and extends the green bar. Clicking left retracts the dot without shrinking the bar. RULE: The bar acts as a one-way trail; it only grows in the direction of movement. TRAP: Believing the bar shrinks when moving left wastes actions. Left clicks only reposition the dot within the existing trail.

GOAL: Move the purple square along the path to the blue destination. CONTROLS: Click dots to move the purple square toward them. RULE: Clicking a dot moves the square up to three steps along the path. TRAP: Clicking distant dots does nothing; you cannot jump more than three steps.

GOAL: Connect the blue ports by aligning the white corridors with the yellow gap. CONTROLS: Clicking a blue port shifts both boundaries: upper left, lower right. RULE: The white path must pass through the fixed yellow marker in the black bar. TRAP: Moving the lower boundary right expanded gray, hiding the path instead of revealing it.

GOAL: Navigate from the start to the target without crossing blocked tiles. CONTROLS: Arrows move two spaces in the chosen direction, skipping the intermediate tile. RULE: You can only move if the tile you land on is passable, regardless of the tile you jump over. TRAP: Assuming you could move one space or that blocked tiles prevented jumping over them.

GOAL: Align the sliding handle with the yellow marker on the bar. CONTROLS: Clicking the port above a bar shifts white from the top corridor to the middle; clicking below shifts white from the middle to the bottom. RULE: Each click transfers four units of white space across the bar, moving the corridor boundary and the attached handle. TRAP: Assuming the handle moves independently; it is fixed to the corridor boundary, so you must shift the entire corridor to position it.

GOAL: Guide the plug down to the U-shaped socket using directional instructions. CONTROLS: Click horizontal or vertical bars to toggle dark/light states; click the ball to execute the sequence. RULE: Dark-dark means DOWN; light-dark means RIGHT; light-light means stay. The piece moves straight, preserving its column. TRAP: Assuming the initial instruction set was the solution. It only moved the plug two cells, requiring three additional toggles to reach the target.

GOAL: Fill the notches by positioning the blue bar under the falling liquid. CONTROLS: Arrows move the bar; Space previews the outcome without committing. RULE: The green bar signals success, but the preview does not update the actual board state. TRAP: Assuming Space finalizes the action; it only simulates, requiring a separate commit method.

GOAL: Arrange seven colored letters into the correct reading sequence. CONTROLS: Click two slots to swap their letters; press space to submit. RULE: Reading order follows the red box, then the green box, then the final red slot. TRAP: Assuming the corridor connects adjacent slots in the sequence; it only marks the transition between boxes.

GOAL: Slide the marker left to the handle using three arrow presses. CONTROLS: Left arrow moved the marker two columns; other arrows did nothing. RULE: Each left press consumed one action but advanced the marker twice as far as a completed round. TRAP: Assuming the marker's width indicated a fixed speed, when it actually changed shape without altering movement.

GOAL: Align three colored handles with their matching markers by transferring height between adjacent pipes. CONTROLS: Clicking a port between two pipes moves one unit of height from the right pipe to the left. RULE: Height is conserved; only the distribution changes, so solve the transfer chain to match all targets simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming you can freely move height in both directions or skip intermediate pipes without checking if the source has enough height.

GOAL: Rotate pink symbols to match blue ones in each column. CONTROLS: Left/Right moved the cursor. Up/Down rotated the selected pink symbol. RULE: Matching colors required identical rotation angles, not just the same symbol shape. TRAP: Assuming the blue strip was fixed or adjustable; it was merely the reference target.

GOAL: Fill the main red grid by replacing blocked slots with pieces from matching colored sub-grids. CONTROLS: Space executes the planned sequence of clicks to move pieces into slots. RULE: A blocked slot’s surrounding frame color dictates which sub-grid’s pieces fill its position. TRAP: Assuming all red slots hold red pieces; blocked slots require green or blue substitutes instead.

GOAL: Guide the marker through the neck to the handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the marker; clicking white cells completes patterns. RULE: Completing the pattern transports the marker through the entire pipe section. TRAP: Assuming arrows are needed to cross the neck; the pattern click did it all.

ESTABLISHED: Snake moves by four-unit steps; SPACE absorbs adjacent boxes. Left box absorbed, growing head to width eight. FAILED: Moving left into empty space did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: Simply absorbing the left box clears the level. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate and translate four units. SPACE absorbs. Right moves bring head toward second box.

GOAL: Insert the tray marker into the red box at slot 3 to splice the green sequence correctly. CONTROLS: Click tray items to select, then click red slots to place. Space submits the arrangement. RULE: The marker’s position in the red box determines where the green items are inserted, replacing that slot. TRAP: Assuming the marker stays in the tray or can be placed anywhere; only slot 3 yields the correct color order.

GOAL: Arrange five red tokens and two blue triplets to match a target sequence. CONTROLS: Click pieces to place them; click markers to insert blue groups into red slots. RULE: Markers duplicate the blue group at their insertion point, allowing identical adjacent triplets. TRAP: Assuming markers split the blue group instead of copying it entirely.

GOAL: Reach the exit without touching the red tile. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one square. RULE: The red tile chases the player if they are within two squares. TRAP: Thinking the red tile flees when close; it actually moves toward you.

GOAL: Fill four boxes using markers and solid pieces, matching each box’s color and pattern. CONTROLS: Click tray items to select, click slots to place. Space confirms the solution. RULE: Each box needs its color marker plus two matching solid pieces in empty slots. TRAP: Assuming markers and pieces are interchangeable. They are distinct items with specific roles.

GOAL: Move the marker to the bottom-left handle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the marker four pixels per press. RULE: The marker travels freely through connected colored regions, ignoring gates. TRAP: Believing the gate required a specific pulse signal to open, rather than being a passable path.

GOAL: Raise the sky bar to clear the orange level. CONTROLS: Click to select a bar; click again to shift it up or down. RULE: Bars stack vertically; the sky must sit above the orange block. TRAP: Assuming the cap stays fixed; it moves with the bar, changing alignment.

GOAL: Arrange markers to read the sequence R b N Y N b R across nested boxes. CONTROLS: Click a piece, then a slot to move it; the displaced piece returns to the tray. RULE: Green pieces occupy the middle three positions, forcing specific nesting of blue and red markers. TRAP: Assuming a unique solution; multiple valid arrangements produce the same sequence, so do not over-analyze positions.

GOAL: Align each cross's center with the intersection of its colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected cross by three pixels; Space switches selection. RULE: A dot is solved when a matching cross arm passes directly through it. TRAP: Assuming one arrow press moves one pixel wasted time; movement is three pixels per press.

GOAL: Move the player to capture three enemies by landing on their cells. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per press. RULE: Landing on an enemy removes it; enemies only attack along their facing lines at distance 2. TRAP: Believing captures require perpendicular arrival; same-row landing also works, saving four actions.

GOAL: Place the midpoint bead on the ring. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move the white dot. Click the green dot to swap positions. RULE: The bead always sits exactly halfway between the two dots. TRAP: Thinking the white dot needed to stay on the ring; moving it away allowed the bead to align.

GOAL: Rotate the ring so the yellow tile aligns with the bracketed position. CONTROLS: Red arrow rotates counterclockwise; green arrow rotates clockwise. RULE: Each click shifts all tiles one step in the arrow's direction. TRAP: Assuming the bracket marks a starting point rather than the target destination.

GOAL: Merge scattered crosses into a single unit by sliding them along empty lines. CONTROLS: Click a cross to select it; click the highlighted target cell to move and absorb other crosses. RULE: Crosses travel straight through empty spaces, stopping only at obstacles or other crosses. TRAP: Assuming alignment in a column solves the level; merging into one is the actual requirement.

GOAL: Move three markers to target positions without overlapping orange dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected marker; Space cycles selection between markers. RULE: Markers are independent; only the selected one moves, and paths must avoid blocked pixels. TRAP: Assuming all markers can be moved in a single continuous sequence; you must switch selection to move each marker separately.

GOAL: Move the piece into the box using a single upward action. CONTROLS: Arrows move the piece one step in the indicated direction. RULE: Alignment with the box allows immediate entry without intermediate steps. TRAP: Assuming the piece was stuck or needed multiple moves; it was already positioned correctly.

ESTABLISHED: Up moves the rail to rows 14-15. Left shifts all blocks left by six columns. Right extends the rail without moving existing blocks. FAILED: Up was blocked when the bottom block aligned with the rightmost block. Moving right did not reposition the blocks. GOAL IS NOT: Simply having the blocks on the upper rail. The specific left-to-right order matters. CONTROLS: Up moves the rail vertically. Left and Right adjust the rail's horizontal position. Down moves the rail to lower rows.

GOAL: Slide crosses to position beads on rings, clearing both chains. CONTROLS: Click a cross to select it; click an empty spot to move the selected cross. RULE: Only the selected cross moves; the bead follows the cross's new position. TRAP: Thinking the active cross stays fixed; you must click each chain's cross to switch control.

GOAL: Make panel D's outer cells red wherever its dial shows blue, matching the other panels. CONTROLS: Click a cell to toggle its color between blue and red. RULE: Red cells are the complement of the dial's gray cells. TRAP: Thinking the dial's gray cells were the targets, rather than the ones to avoid.

GOAL: Move three markers—H, X, and D—to cover eight scattered dots. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the selected marker; Space cycles selection between markers. RULE: Markers absorb dots they touch; overlapping coverage is allowed and efficient. TRAP: Assuming markers only move horizontally like level 2; the H marker moves vertically too.

GOAL: Move the yellow tile to the target by rotating three linked loops. CONTROLS: Click green arrows to rotate loops forward; red arrows rotate backward. RULE: Tiles shift one position per click; the yellow tile travels through intersecting loops. TRAP: Assuming rotations are independent; moving the yellow tile requires coordinating multiple loops to avoid losing progress.

GOAL: Make the fourth dial's red lights match the pattern shown by the other three dials. CONTROLS: Clicking a light on the fourth dial toggles its color between red and blue. RULE: Red lights appear where the other dials show white, not gray, excluding the center. TRAP: Assuming the bottom-right light was correct; the target required the bottom-left instead.

ESTABLISHED: Balls move through the black maze, not the pipes. Yellow and orange pipes connect at a gap in the upper black bar. FAILED: Moving balls to flank the connection gap did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply positioning balls adjacent to the pipe junction. CONTROLS: Directional inputs move both balls simultaneously through open black cells; walls block movement without penalty.

GOAL: Place the white token in the left socket and the cyan token in the right socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move the white token. Clicking a token swaps its color with the white token. RULE: Clicking swaps colors without moving positions, allowing you to fix token placement after moving them. TRAP: Assuming arrows move any token; they only move the white token, requiring clicks to reposition others.

GOAL: Match dial patterns to neighbor colors, updating dials after painting. CONTROLS: Click cells to paint; click dials to rotate patterns. RULE: Dials encode neighbor states; gray means "not this dial's color." TRAP: Assuming painted cells don't require dial updates; they do, or patterns become inconsistent.

GOAL: Move yellow to L13 and orange to R5. CONTROLS: Left and right buttons rotate specific tile groups. RULE: Each tile’s position changes independently under the same action, so track only their pair. TRAP: Assuming other tiles’ positions affect the solution wastes time; they are irrelevant.

GOAL: Clear the level by moving the two balls to specific target locations, likely the junctions or symmetric points in the hourglass maze. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both balls simultaneously in the selected direction. RULE: The balls merge when adjacent, sharing the same cell, which simplifies movement but obscures individual positions. TRAP: Assuming the goal was simply to merge the balls at the top junction; they merged there without clearing the level.

ESTABLISHED: The blue block eats red by moving right to (8,38), causing the red line to shift left, overwriting white cells. The red snake connects to the horizontal line via rows 38 and 42. FAILED: Repeatedly moving right and left at the top-right position does not permanently advance the red snake or reveal new paths. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the hollow square, as the bottom section remains unreachable from the top-left component. CONTROLS: Right moves the blue block and triggers eating; Left restores the red line.

GOAL: Guide the bead 82 units along a fixed path using four movable crosses as waypoints. CONTROLS: Click to select a cross; click again to set its new position for the next jump. RULE: Each jump must land on a valid grid point, with crosses spaced far enough apart to avoid collisions. TRAP: Assuming the bead can change direction freely; it follows a rigid path, so only jump lengths are adjustable.

GOAL: Fill the grid so each dial's neighbors match its rule, using three colors. CONTROLS: Click cells to cycle colors; observe dial indicators for equality or inequality constraints. RULE: Dials marked with a slash require neighbors to differ from the center, not just be "the other" color. TRAP: Assuming "not center" means a single specific color; with three colors, it allows two options, requiring careful selection to satisfy all dials.

GOAL: Move yellow and orange tiles to specific intersection points on the grid lines. CONTROLS: Click arrows to shift tiles along the horizontal or vertical cycles. RULE: The two lines form single 20-tile loops sharing four center tiles; shifts wrap around. TRAP: Treating the two columns as separate 10-tile cycles instead of one connected loop.

GOAL: Align white prongs with green pins by moving the plug down and right. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the white piece three cells per press. RULE: Prongs must touch pins without overlapping the green body. TRAP: Assuming the plug inserts into the green hollow; it connects externally.

GOAL: Place numbered tokens into matching sockets by moving them across the grid. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected token; clicks select a token and swap its status marker with the previously selected one. RULE: Tokens can only move when holding the specific status marker required for their destination socket. TRAP: Believing tokens block each other’s paths; they actually stack, allowing one to push another through bands to reach distant targets.

GOAL: Turn specific cells pink to match dial constraints using a toggle puzzle. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles colors in a cross pattern. RULE: Cross-cells retain their toggle shape even when color changes. TRAP: Assuming toggles reset cross-shapes led to invalid moves; the geometry is fixed, only the color flips.

GOAL: Move the black piece onto the yellow target using only horizontal shifts. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the black piece three cells per press. RULE: The yellow piece marks the destination; orientation must match the target. TRAP: Assuming vertical movement was allowed; the piece only slides left or right.

GOAL: Rotate the purple piece to the bottom position to match the reference layout. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the piece counter-clockwise along its orbit, but only if the arrow direction matched the movement's displacement. RULE: The piece advanced only when the input arrow aligned with the next step's direction; mismatched inputs did nothing. TRAP: Assuming DOWN always advances the piece; at the diagonal position, only RIGHT moved it to the final spot.

GOAL: Paint the square to match the reference pattern using colored pieces. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the piece around the square; Space paints the half-plane defined by the piece's position and color. RULE: The last paint applied overwrites previous colors in the overlapping area. TRAP: Assuming paint layers are additive or transparent; they are opaque, so order matters critically.

GOAL: Guide beads along colored tracks to matching endpoints, connecting chains without breaking solved links. CONTROLS: Click a cross to select it; click the next cross in its chain to move the bead. RULE: Only adjacent crosses in the same color chain can connect; the active bead blocks its own track. TRAP: Missing an active cross because its connecting line pixels merged with it, hiding it from the filtered list.

ESTABLISHED: Green is confined to the left column; red, dark red, and yellow cells block movement. The horizontal bar and vertical red connector are impassable walls. FAILED: Random walks and rightward attempts from the bottom box failed to reach the top box or the yellow token. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the yellow token or connecting the bottom box to the top box via the bar. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move green within passable gray and blue cells. No other controls altered the level state.

GOAL: Move the divider to align the black piece's reflection with the yellow target. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows shift the divider horizontally; the black piece stays fixed. RULE: The divider acts as a mirror; moving it changes the reflection's position without moving the source. TRAP: Assuming arrows move the black piece or that the reflection can reach the yellow's original location.

GOAL: Guide two balls to share one cell without touching red blocks. CONTROLS: Arrows move both balls simultaneously; blocked moves are ignored. RULE: Only black cells are passable; red blocks act as walls for both. TRAP: Assuming adjacent balls win; they must occupy the exact same cell.

GOAL: Position the cross so its bars align exactly with the empty socket outlines. CONTROLS: Arrows move the square carrier; pushing an adjacent cross makes it jump far in that direction. RULE: The carrier does not stick to the cross; it pushes once, then the cross slides independently until it hits a wall or another piece. TRAP: Assuming the carrier drags the cross along. It does not; you must reposition the carrier to push again.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking items removes them without score or player movement. The world scrolls up as the player rises. FAILED: Removing items did not trigger passage opening, score changes, or level completion. GOAL IS NOT: Collecting items for points or simple item removal. CONTROLS: Right/left arrows move the player horizontally. Up/down arrows adjust vertical position. Clicking items deletes them.

GOAL: Mirror two charcoal shapes onto yellow targets using a central divider. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected piece; Space switched selection or moved the divider. RULE: Shapes reflect across the divider; align reflections to cover yellow outlines. TRAP: Moving pieces directly onto targets failed; only reflections could cover them.

GOAL: Align three pieces and a divider so reflections cover four yellow markers. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece or divider. Space cycles which one is active. RULE: Reflections are mirrored across the divider line; only the final alignment counts. TRAP: Thinking the divider must stay put. Moving it shifts all reflections, which is necessary.

GOAL: Open a passage through the wall and guide the player to the pink marker. CONTROLS: Clicking items removes them to clear paths. Arrow keys move the player; moving into an open column causes an automatic rise. RULE: The player only rises through columns where the wall has been fully removed. TRAP: Assuming removal alone moves the player. You must also navigate horizontally to align with the new opening.

GOAL: Raise the water in the second pocket to align the handle with the marker in the third bar. CONTROLS: Clicking the third column transfers water to the second pocket. Clicking the orange gate moves the handle into the second pocket. RULE: The gate opens only when adjacent water levels match exactly. TRAP: Assuming the handle needs to touch the bar; alignment by row is sufficient.

GOAL: Guide the player from the bottom-left to the top-right, avoiding the oscillating guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one tile per turn, simultaneously with the guard. RULE: The guard bounces vertically between rows 0 and 8; the player must not occupy any tile the guard passes through during its movement. TRAP: Assuming the guard stops at row 2 instead of continuing to row 0 led to incorrect collision predictions and wasted moves.

GOAL: Route two pieces to cover matching dots without touching wrong color squares. CONTROLS: Arrows move pieces; Space selects the active piece. RULE: Pieces change color only when their arms overlap a square, not the piece itself. TRAP: Moving straight back through a previously visited square re-triggers its color change.

GOAL: Clear the board by filling all cells with matching colors. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selection cursor. Clicks apply the selected color to the highlighted region. Space cycles the active color. RULE: Paints overwrite previous colors completely; the final layer determines the visible result. TRAP: Assuming overlapping shapes create intersections or blends. They simply replace the underlying cells.

GOAL: Reach the exit tile while avoiding moving hazards. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one step per turn. RULE: Hazards bounce off walls; their paths repeat in fixed cycles. TRAP: Assuming hazards travel in straight lines ignores their reflections.

GOAL: Fill three containers with liquid without overflowing into the ceiling. CONTROLS: Arrows moved colored bars; clicks adjusted width; space poured liquid. RULE: Streams only fill containers when landing directly on notch columns; otherwise, they overflow. TRAP: Believing adjacent streams would merge or fill correctly; misaligned columns caused ceiling overflow instead of filling.

GOAL: Move the cross to fill the top socket. CONTROLS: Arrows push adjacent tokens; clicks select the active piece. RULE: Pushing a piece into another moves the target, not the pusher. TRAP: Assuming blocked pushes are no-ops; they can displace the pusher or fail silently, wasting moves.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding moving orange barriers and static red traps. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one square per action. RULE: Orange barriers oscillate along specific lines; timing passage between their positions is key. TRAP: Assuming red traps are always active; they remain static until triggered by proximity or action.

ESTABLISHED: SPACE rotates the W piece 90 degrees clockwise around its center. LEFT shifts it three pixels. The piece is a rigid T-shape. FAILED: Repeated SPACE cycles orientation without clearing. Additional LEFT shifts after rotation did not solve the puzzle. GOAL IS NOT: Simply rotating the piece to a specific angle or translating it left. CONTROLS: SPACE rotates. LEFT moves. DOWN moves down. MOUSE clicks at step 32.

GOAL: Divide the grid into blue, orange, and purple regions using diagonal boundaries. CONTROLS: Click outer edges to paint lines; click center to select colors. RULE: Painted lines overwrite previous colors, allowing you to adjust boundaries by layering. TRAP: Assuming lines are additive; they actually replace existing colors in the affected area.

GOAL: Join six pairs of tips into joints without overlapping bodies. CONTROLS: Click to select a shape. Arrows translate it. Space rotates it. RULE: Only the selected shape moves; others stay fixed, blocking paths. TRAP: Moving the white shape away from the yellow shape's hidden tips obscured the connection points, wasting time on blind moves.

GOAL: Guide the green token through the narrow channel to the exit socket. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the token; pushing against walls or bars stops motion. RULE: The token drills through colored bars, leaving white holes, but cannot pass orange barriers. TRAP: Assuming bars block movement permanently; they actually yield to repeated pushes.

GOAL: Fill the triangle with blue, leaving a red strip. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cursor; Space painted the selected color; Click applied the red strip. RULE: Later paints overwrite earlier ones. Orange must be painted last to cover the diagonal. TRAP: Assuming paint order didn’t matter. Painting blue, then orange, then blue overwrote the orange edge, requiring a redo.

GOAL: Move green to pocket three and yellow to pocket zero by swapping them across an open gate. CONTROLS: Click gates to move handles; click ports to transfer energy between adjacent pockets. RULE: Clicking an open gate moves every handle adjacent to it to the opposite pocket simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming gates move only one handle at a time caused failed attempts to position both colors correctly.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while evading a pursuer that closes the gap when you drift too far. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one tile per press; the enemy moves automatically after each turn. RULE: The enemy only moves if the distance between you exceeds two steps; staying close keeps it stationary. TRAP: Assuming the enemy always advances wastes moves; hovering nearby safely blocks its path.

GOAL: Send a pink pulse down the corridor to absorb the M block. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the two-tone marker; clicks fired the pulse. RULE: The pulse travels in the direction of the marker's black half. TRAP: Assuming the pulse follows the previous movement or the marker's center, rather than its orientation.

GOAL: Guide two balls to meet in the connected maze. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both balls simultaneously. RULE: Mirrored movement: right-side ball moves opposite to left-side ball. TRAP: Assuming independent control or sequential solving wastes actions; simultaneous, mirrored motion is mandatory.

GOAL: Rotate and move three colored pieces to connect their tips into a closed triangle. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it. Arrows move the selected piece. Space rotates it. RULE: A solution exists if all piece tips pair up without overlap, forming a continuous loop. TRAP: Assuming pieces stay in place while others move. They are independent; moving one does not affect the others' positions.

GOAL: Move the handle to the right edge by aligning panel widths with gates. CONTROLS: Click ports to transfer width between adjacent panels; click gates to move the handle. RULE: Gates only open when connected panels have equal widths. TRAP: Assuming the handle stays in place after crossing a gate; it moves to the next panel, requiring further width adjustments to reach the target.

GOAL: Move the black piece to the top-left target by adjusting divider positions before cycling them to a movable state. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the active divider; SPACE cycles the active divider through Horizontal, Vertical, and Piece modes. RULE: Only the divider in Piece mode allows arrow moves to translate the piece; other modes adjust the grid. TRAP: Assuming the piece moved right when adjusting the vertical divider; it stayed at column 42, requiring extra left moves.

GOAL: Move two same-color pieces into range to merge, then deliver the result to the target. CONTROLS: Click empty space to spawn a piece; click near a piece to move it toward that spot. RULE: Pieces merge when within distance 6 of each other upon landing, not just when touching. TRAP: Believing pieces must be adjacent to merge; they merged across a 4-row gap, saving clicks.

ESTABLISHED: Orange and pink bars interact with walls to redirect paths; sky dot must align with crosshairs. FAILED: Placing orange+wall below pink blocks sky; pushing wall left extends orange, blocking sky anyway. GOAL IS NOT: Simply covering crosshairs without managing vertical overlap of orange, wall, and sky. CONTROLS: Arrow keys push bars; orange extends left, moving attached wall; pink extends or shifts based on collisions.

ESTABLISHED: The win requires liquid to fill the entire top region contiguously. The L2 solution used stacked bars covering the middle columns to intercept sources and spread liquid across gaps. FAILED: Single-move hill-climbing and empirical configuration testing did not produce a contiguous fill. The no-op guard interfered with batch testing. GOAL IS NOT: Simply maximizing top-row liquid coverage without ensuring contiguity. CONTROLS: LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN move bars or the source. SPACE simulates liquid flow. There is no UNDO.

GOAL: Place each piece onto its matching colored blob, aligning them to the target pattern shown in the bar. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell moves the selected piece so its top-left corner lands one row up and one column left of the click. RULE: Completion requires every piece to be centered on a blob, not merely touching its edge or surface. TRAP: Believing overlap alone suffices; pieces resting on the blob’s perimeter fail to trigger the win condition.

GOAL: Guide the piece to the matching icon by collecting three hits to shift the HUD pattern, using yellow squares to refill the movement bar. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the piece one step; hitting yellow squares restores bar length. RULE: Each hit rotates the HUD icon sequence; match the box icon to exit. TRAP: Assuming the bar lasts without refilling; skipping yellow squares strands you before the exit.

GOAL: Guide two balls to the same cell to merge them. CONTROLS: Arrows move all balls simultaneously; clicks select a ball or deselect the token. RULE: Balls stop at obstacles or tokens, allowing independent positioning before merging. TRAP: Assuming the yellow background is walkable terrain; only black cells and object footprints are valid.

GOAL: Guide the blue X to cover all blue dots, then move the diamond to the red target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space switches selection between shapes. RULE: The X covers dots on its entire arms, not just its center position. TRAP: Assuming the X must stop exactly on each dot; it only needs to pass through them.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking green items opens adjacent black separators. RIGHT moves the player six units right, clearing a path that follows it while restoring cells behind. Purple items are lethal. FAILED: Analyzing camera movement models and periodicity hypotheses consumed budget without clarifying the map transformation. GOAL IS NOT: A static P marker appearing upon simple item removal, as seen in Level 1. CONTROLS: Click to interact with items. RIGHT to move and drill through walls. Other directions untested.

GOAL: Fill the bar’s window with three dots to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; space absorbs or deposits dots into the head. RULE: Only dots placed inside the window count toward the solution. TRAP: Assuming the player’s position in the window contributes to the fill.

GOAL: Guide the node along the pipe to panel B. CONTROLS: Click arrows to move; click nodes to select. RULE: Movement follows the pipe; DOWN at (4,4) is blocked. TRAP: Assuming adjacent crosses interact; they do not.

GOAL: Reach the yellow tile in the top box. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green piece; clicking podiums toggles wall colors. RULE: Blue paths allow movement; checker patterns block passage. TRAP: Toggling walls does not move the piece—plan the full path before switching colors.

ESTABLISHED: The plug moves up four cells, stopping at the cup's rim. Extra up-instructions do nothing. Column four accepts horizontal commands. FAILED: Repeated up-movements to force a merge. GOAL IS NOT: Simply stacking the plug vertically on the cup. CONTROLS: Horizontal bars set left or right moves. Vertical bars set up or down. Clicking a bar toggles its state.

GOAL: Rotate the target box 90 degrees clockwise by covering the crosshair twice, then moving to the finish. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the piece; covering the crosshair triggers rotation; moving to the target box completes the level. RULE: Each hit rotates the box clockwise; two hits align it with the goal. TRAP: Assuming the portal at the right cap works immediately; it requires precise positioning to activate, wasting moves if guessed.

ESTABLISHED: Yellow tiles remain trapped in their initial upper or lower groups. Clicking bracket markers does nothing. The partition between groups appears permanent. FAILED: Clicking arrows at various positions, clicking bracket markers, and multiple rotation sequences failed to bridge the groups or clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Filling both upper brackets with two yellow tiles, as the lower yellow cannot reach the top group. CONTROLS: R and A rotate or permute tiles within the existing groups without crossing boundaries.

GOAL: Align a seven-piece yellow strip to match a four-piece pink strip. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the active piece along the strip. RULE: The number of yellow pieces per color encoded the pink piece’s rotation angle. TRAP: Assuming yellow piece counts matched pink indices directly wasted time on incorrect sequences.

GOAL: Guide the blue token to the exit while avoiding the ghost's path. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the token one step per press. SPACE resets the current attempt and restores the move budget. RULE: The ghost holds position after reaching its limit, allowing the token to pass safely during the pause. TRAP: Assuming the move budget is a global counter rather than a per-attempt resource led to wasted resets and confusion.

GOAL: Guide the plug to the top bar using four directional commands. CONTROLS: Click grid intersections to toggle horizontal or vertical barriers. Click the ball to run the program. RULE: Commands execute in column order, moving the plug through open gaps between barriers. TRAP: Assuming the fourth UP command moves the plug; it actually stalls against the top barrier.

GOAL: Move the plug to the cup by passing through the magenta wall. CONTROLS: Click matrix bars to set movement directions; click the ball to execute the sequence. RULE: The magenta wall is passable; the plug moves through it without stopping or changing state. TRAP: Believing the wall blocks movement or requires removal wastes actions testing alternatives.

GOAL: Guide the node to capture all crosses on the pipe. CONTROLS: Click adjacent cells to move; click crosses to select and capture targets. RULE: Nodes and crosses capture each other by jumping over adjacent pieces into empty spaces. TRAP: Assuming fixed screen coordinates ignores camera scrolling, leading to wrong movement calculations.

GOAL: Cycle the piece through four colors to match the target pattern before delivery. CONTROLS: Arrows move; entering the center object advances the color. RULE: Colors rotate in a fixed sequence, not random swaps. TRAP: Thinking the object maps colors independently; it actually shifts the current state along a single loop.

ESTABLISHED: The 2x2 marker traverses the horizontal arm; LEFT moves it along the arm. RIGHT is blocked at the arm's right end. The 4x4 marker cannot fit the arm. FAILED: Attempting to reach the bottom M-block or remove the O-center via the p-gate. Oscillating UP/DOWN at the gate. GOAL IS NOT: Simply removing the O-center from the bottom block, nor clearing the corridor's O independently. CONTROLS: LEFT moves the marker along the arm. RIGHT is blocked. UP/DOWN are blocked at the gate. Pink pulse requires alignment with an M.

ESTABLISHED: The target is a six-color sequence. The red box expands recursively, splicing blue pieces into its own slots. FAILED: Assuming the target is twelve colors or requiring a specific depth limit for truncation. GOAL IS NOT: Matching a twelve-item sequence or using a fixed recursion depth. CONTROLS: Placing markers in red slots inserts blue contents; blue markers insert red contents. No other actions observed.

ESTABLISHED: Green can traverse the left column, cross to the pink bar, and reach the bottom box via the vertical pink path. FAILED: Reaching the bottom box did not complete the level; the red bump is not the exit. GOAL IS NOT: The bottom box is not the destination. CONTROLS: P toggles blue/checker patterns; U/D/L/R move green; pink rotates around magenta pivot.

GOAL: Guide the green token to the yellow target within a strict action limit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the token; clicking podiums rotates them to form connecting bridges. RULE: Bridges only link when adjacent segments align at matching heights. TRAP: Assuming the red podium click failed when it actually succeeded, just before the time ran out.
